newsitem.title: FRANCE: French direct mail mogul on trial for swindle.
newsitem.headline: French direct mail mogul on trial for swindle.

text.p: The head of a major French direct mail firm went on trial on Monday, accused of selling useless gadgets and failing to deliver on promises of giving enticing prizes.
Bernard Graeff, chairman of France Direct Service (FDS) and other companies, faced charges of swindle, deceit, bankruptcy and misuse of corporate funds.
The state prosecutor accuses him of "promising fabulous gains through various games in order to sell goods which were mostly poor-quality imported gadgets".

He said gullible customers believed they would automatically win cars or exotic holidays if they ordered goods. Some received a Chinese-made pocket gadget closer to a stapler than to the sewing machine they had expected.
Many of the gadgets paid for were never delivered at all as stocks ran out.
The court in the southern town of Grasse had to move to the local congress hall to accommodate crowds of plaintiffs. But only 66 of the 15,134 clients who sued Graeff turned up for the trial.
Graeff has been convicted twice previously of deceitful advertising. In view of the large number of plaintiffs, the court is expected to take several months to deliver its verdict.
